t: You're looking at St Pancras New Church, a Greek Revival building put up between 1819 and 1822 to designs by William and Henry William Inwood. It's regarded as one of the most important nineteenth-century churches in England, it's Grade One listed, and it's still a working place of worship, with services at eleven on Sundays. It's also the principal church for the Borough of Camden, which holds its civic services here. The name comes from Saint Pancras, a Roman citizen who converted to Christianity and was beheaded for his faith at fourteen, around the year 304. Among those buried here is the writer John Mason Good.
